tagline: Pines, mountain meadows and desert views line a road built in 1937.
intro: Sunrise Highway threads the Laguna Mountains through pine, spruce and fir, with mountain meadows and views down to the desert. The National Forest Scenic Byway follows the portion of County Route S1 north of Interstate 8. The Forest Service highlights the woodland drive and its overlooks, including Desert View’s outlook over terrain 6,000 feet below. The forest becomes denser as the highway gains elevation from Interstate 8, with campgrounds beside the road. Picnic areas and the Penny Pines monument provide day-hike connections to the Pacific Crest Trail.

Construction of Sunrise Highway in 1937 used the flat at Pine Valley Overlook as a borrow pit. The road passed through a forest already served by El Prado Cabin, built in 1912 and for many years Cleveland National Forest’s only station. Its ranger handled fire lookout, grazing permits and camping.

Begin at Highway 79 near Lake Cuyamaca and follow the road south toward Mount Laguna. The hamlet occupies the high point of the drive, approximately 6,000 feet above sea level among Jeffrey pines. Penny Pines, El Prado Cabin and Desert View offer stops along the way. Toward Interstate 8, the road descends through chaparral and sagebrush along a cliff overlooking Pine Valley to the west.

moments.title: Penny Pines
moments.text: Children and organizations collect and give pennies each year for planting in the national forest. A monument at Penny Pines honors their contributions. A short walk behind the monument reaches a penny pine plantation. The turnout also provides access to the Noble Canyon National Recreation Trail and Big Laguna Trail, while day hikers can reach the Pacific Crest Trail from the monument.
moments.notice: A short walk behind the monument reaches a penny pine plantation.

moments.title: El Prado Cabin
moments.text: El Prado Cabin was built in 1912 with just one room of logs. For many years it served as Cleveland National Forest’s only national forest station. The ranger’s duties ranged from fire lookout to grazing permits and camping. The cabin is in Laguna Campground, just off the byway.

moments.title: Desert View Picnic Area
moments.text: Desert View looks down 6,000 feet to the desert from a road that passes through pine, spruce and fir. On most days, the Salton Sea is visible to the southeast. This picnic area is also one of the byway’s access points for day hikers on the Pacific Crest Trail.
